title: With the Five Pine Groves
text:
With the five pine groves of your death and mine

you will return. Listen. The promise kissed

upon your traceless scar with its silent cluster

gives us destiny and fruit in the wound of the air.

If I could give you belief and the years,

the renewed vision this autumn afternoon,

dazzled and certain, without cowardly memory,

sickly vileness, without solitude or help...

It is love returning. And what do we do now

if the dawn lark is singing in the resin

of the five pine groves of your death and mine?

It was too soon, but now it is not late.

If it is love without an owner, if it is our creation:

the mystery that saves, and the life that lives!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's recurring pine groves as a shared place of death, return, and salvaging love.

title: You Have No Other Name
text:
You have no other name beyond yourself


Among the names of the poppy and the violet,

among all the names of the ring,

I prefer the word shared in silence.


To live, I ask to know no more names.


It is enough to know that it is revealed

when breast rests upon breast

and limbs intertwine like the vine,

when hands recover their embraces

and pubises mingle where iron is forged.


The most exact name, the summit point,

is revealed in a time without memory,

and pores half-open to other pores,

and eyes melt little by little.


Like the shell kissed by foam,

you have no other name beyond yourself.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's erotic naming through silence, touch, and bodily revelation.

title: Someone Said That Laughter...
text:
Someone said that "laughter

is the great burier."

Something is being buried in me

because I laugh at every hour.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Méndez's compact paradox of laughter as a sign of hidden burial.

title: Midnight
text:
Midnight.

Black song.

And my only star is singing!...


Let them break that clock

and leave me alone with her!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the lyric as a midnight wish to stop time and remain with the singing star.

title: Pure Water Ran...
text:
Pure water ran

through the piano.

Sweetly it flowed

from the channel of her hands.


Nostalgia slept.

And the West slept.

Music was drinking

the water from its glass.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the piano image as water moving through hands while music drinks from its own glass.
